edits.old: For a multi-region restore, local copies in the target cluster's regions can allow Atlas to use faster direct-attach restores when the target is in the same project and regions as those copies. If a local copy is unavailable or the target uses NVMe storage, Atlas defaults to slower streaming restore; snapshot distribution therefore does not guarantee a fixed restore time. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23)
edits.new: If you copy snapshots to every region in a multi-region cluster, Atlas can perform faster direct attach restores instead of slower streaming restores after a regional outage. For faster cross-project restores, a multi-region target should be used only if copies of the snapshot exist in every region of that cluster, and a target configured with NVMe storage degrades restore performance. Snapshot distribution therefore does not guarantee a fixed restore time. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/backup/cloud-backup/snapshot-distribution.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/backup/cloud-backup/restore-from-snapshot.md

evidence.quote: You can now choose exactly which snapshots to copy to your disaster recovery regions rather than being forced to copy each one within a frequency unit.
We have decoupled the retention settings for the copy from those of the original. You can now set unique retention periods for snapshot copies in each region.
you can now retroactively apply those changes to snapshots that have already been copied.
* `last_number_of_snapshots` - (Optional) Number of most recent snapshots to copy, from 1 to 500, when `copy_policy_items_enabled` is true.
* `delete_copy_snapshots` - (Optional) Specify true to delete snapshot copies when their associated `copy_policy_items` are removed.
* `update_copy_snapshots` - (Optional) Specify true to apply the retention changes for updated copy policy items to snapshot copies that Atlas took previously.
